sentences.zh: 当你试图用任何东西来取代它们时，你面临的最大问题是，这有点像民主制度。

sentences.en: There's a lot of critiques of democracy at the moment.
sentences.zh: 目前对民主制度有很多批评。

sentences.en: What are you going to do instead of them?
sentences.zh: 那你打算用什么来代替它们呢？

sentences.en: And when you all of the alternatives you come up with seem to have all the flaws of exams, plus some new ones.
sentences.zh: 当你提出的所有替代方案似乎都具备考试的所有缺陷，甚至还有一些新的缺陷时。

sentences.en: So what you've seen this year and last year with the teacher assessment
sentences.zh: 所以你今年和去年在教师评估中看到的情况是，

sentences.en: is that teacher assessment, many issues with it, I think, but one of the big issues you have with it
sentences.zh: 教师评估，我认为它有很多问题，但你面临的一个大问题是，

sentences.en: is that poorer students, disadvantaged students, students with behavioural issues, students with
sentences.zh: 贫困学生、弱势学生、有行为问题的学生、有

sentences.en: special educational needs, all tend to do worse on teacher assessment than on exaMs. And people are often really surprised when I say that.
sentences.zh: 特殊教育需求的学生，在教师评估中的表现往往比在考试中更差。人们听到我这么说时通常感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: They say, no, it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，情况正好相反。

sentences.en: You're wrong.
sentences.zh: 你错了。

sentences.en: It must be the other way around.
sentences.zh: 情况一定是相反的。

sentences.en: And it's not.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: There's a huge research body on this.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有大量的研究。

sentences.en: And it's to do with similarly big research bodies on human bias.
sentences.zh: 这与关于人类偏见的大量研究结论是一致的。

sentences.en: And the thing I say, teachers are biased not because they're bad people, they're biased because they're human.
sentences.zh: 我常说，老师有偏见不是因为他们是坏人，而是因为他们是人。

sentences.en: And lots of things that involve human judgment do have those biases built into them.
sentences.zh: 许多涉及人类判断的事情确实内置了这些偏见。

sentences.en: So as I say, that's one of the best evidence findings in the assessment literature.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我所说，这是评估文献中最好的研究发现之一。

sentences.en: So the great problem you have if you want to rely on just the kind of pure teacher assessment we've had in these past two years, as we've had it because of necessity,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想完全依赖我们过去两年中那种纯粹的教师评估——我们是因为必要才采用它的——你面临的最大问题是，

sentences.en: is that it doesn't really give you that level playing field.
sentences.zh: 它并不能真正提供公平的竞争环境。

sentences.en: And exams certainly have their probleMs. And I'm not pretending that exams are the perfectly level playing field either.
sentences.zh: 考试当然也有它们的问题。我并不是说考试就是完美的公平竞争环境。

sentences.en: But again, it's, I'd say of all the different alternatives, they're the ones that are probably
sentences.zh: 但同样，我会说在所有不同的替代方案中，它们可能是

sentences.en: the beSt. So I think there are lots of people who are saying, well, the pandemic shows that we've got to change things.
sentences.zh: 最好的。所以我认为有很多人说，疫情表明我们必须做出改变。

sentences.en: But my argument would be the pandemic shows us that when we can't run exams, we have real probleMs. So I would say I think we need them.
sentences.zh: 但我的观点是，疫情向我们表明，当我们无法进行考试时，我们会有真正的问题。所以我认为我们需要考试。

sentences.en: And I think we'll still be using them in years to come.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在未来的几年里，我们仍将使用它们。

sentences.en: And so just on the back of that, kind of looking at the broad context of what we've been talking
sentences.zh: 那么，基于这一点，回顾我们一直在讨论的广泛背景，

sentences.en: about generally, do you think in the future that exams will serve the cause of social mobility
sentences.zh: 你认为未来考试会促进社会流动性，

sentences.en: or entrench existing divisions?
sentences.zh: 还是会固化现有的阶层分化？

sentences.en: So that is a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And it is hard to say.
sentences.zh: 很难说。

sentences.en: And as I say, I don't want to pretend that exams are perfect, and that they are this perfect engine of social mobility.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我不想假装考试是完美的，也不想说它们是促进社会流动性的完美引擎。

sentences.en: Again, I think it is really interesting to look back to China, where I think you can argue that there's a phase in their history
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为回顾中国历史非常有趣，我认为你可以说在他们历史的某个阶段，

sentences.en: where they probably were working as you would want them to work.
sentences.zh: 考试可能确实发挥了你所期望的作用。

sentences.en: And then there was a phase where they weren't.
sentences.zh: 然后有一个阶段它们没有发挥作用。

sentences.en: And I think you can see something similar, probably in the modern Western system of
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以在现代西方考试制度中看到类似的情况，

sentences.en: exams, that you can see there are ways where they do work as they're meant to, there are ways where they don't.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它们在某些方面确实按预期发挥了作用，而在某些方面则没有。

sentences.en: I think there are real issues around the content of what should be on exams, and whether what is on exams is preparing students for the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为考试内容本身存在真正的问题，以及考试内容是否在为学生进入社会做准备。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely a legitimate question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一个合理的问题。

sentences.en: So I think that you want reform of that, that seems to me it can be sensible.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你想要对此进行改革，这在我看来是明智的。

sentences.en: I think the other big issue you have as well is, yeah, I think there is an issue around if they do just become, if you like, box ticking, hoop jumping exercises.
sentences.zh: 我认为你面临的另一个大问题是，是的，我认为如果它们仅仅变成了一种打勾、跳圈式的练习，确实存在问题。

sentences.en: And I think if you do get too much almost kind of over reliance on rubrics, I think that can decay confidence in them.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为如果你对评分标准过于依赖，我认为这会削弱人们对考试的信心。

sentences.en: And I think that also means they're probably not doing their job of actually giving students the knowledge and skills they need to get by in the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这也意味着它们可能没有完成赋予学生在社会中生存所需的知识和技能的任务。

sentences.en: So they become almost something that's separate from the education, they can become a bit detached from it, they become a means, you know, a means to an end on their own.
sentences.zh: 所以它们几乎变得与教育本身分离开来，它们可能变得有点脱节，它们本身就变成了一种手段，你知道，一种为了达到目的的手段。

sentences.en: I think that is a real problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's the kind of thing, we talked about this happening in China, where you then can get that dominance of them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们谈到的在中国发生的情况，在那里你会看到考试的主导地位。

sentences.en: And I think there's that feeling that, well, you know, maybe private schools have this secret, secret sauce where they can just get
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有一种感觉是，嗯，你知道，也许私立学校有什么秘方，能让他们的学生

sentences.en: their pupils to kind of jump through these hoops.
sentences.zh: 跳过这些圈。

sentences.en: So I think it is really important that they're fair and there's a level playing field.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为考试公平并提供公平的竞争环境非常重要。

sentences.en: And I think it's really important they're perceived to have that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为让人们感知到这一点也非常重要。

sentences.en: And I certainly think there's ways we could reform them so that they do a better job there.
sentences.zh: 我当然认为我们可以通过改革让它们做得更好。

sentences.en: And I do share the concerns of people who say, if we don't make some of those reforms, then it's not just a
sentences.zh: 我也确实认同那些人的担忧，他们说，如果我们不进行一些改革，那么这不仅是

sentences.en: problem for the exam system, but it is a problem for society because of that outsized role that exams play in our life.
sentences.zh: 考试系统的问题，更是社会的问题，因为考试在我们生活中扮演着过大的角色。

sentences.en: But Tom, if elite overproduction is your concern, and you think that elite overproduction leads to unrest, right, then greater social mobility in exams wouldn't solve that.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，如果精英过剩是你的担忧，并且你认为精英过剩会导致动荡，对吧，那么考试中更大的社会流动性并不能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: It would just mean a different part of the overproduced elite was satisfied.
sentences.zh: 那只会意味着过剩精英中的另一部分得到了满足。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Peter Turchin, his argument is you don't want to be making, you don't want to be getting all these meritocrats striving for the top role.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得·图尔钦（Peter Turchin）的观点是，你不想制造，你不想让所有这些精英都在争夺最高职位。

sentences.en: You actually need some way of damping down competition.
sentences.zh: 你实际上需要某种方式来抑制竞争。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He takes that quite kind of counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 他采取了相当反直觉的态度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would say the implication of that argument is actually just educate, stop educating so many people.
sentences.zh: 我会说这个论点的含义实际上就是：教育，停止教育那么多人。

sentences.en: Because that just, I mean, you could laugh, but that's surely the obvious conclusion, right?
sentences.zh: 因为那只会……我的意思是，你可以笑，但这肯定是最明显的结论，对吧？

sentences.en: Unless you're going to magically create the jobs for the people to go to, then if elite overproduction is your fear, then the issue is elite overproduction.
sentences.zh: 除非你能神奇地创造出工作岗位供人们去填补，否则如果精英过剩是你的恐惧，那么问题就在于精英过剩。

sentences.en: I stopped producing so many elite people.
sentences.zh: 停止培养那么多精英。

sentences.en: Or produce more elite jobs.
sentences.zh: 或者创造更多精英职位。

sentences.en: Well, you can't just, unless you've got, are you blessed with the magic wand that would create elite jobs out of nowhere?
sentences.zh: 除非你拥有某种能凭空创造精英职位的魔法棒，否则你不能只靠空想，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's why I need to become a dictator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么我需要成为一名独裁者。

sentences.en: The other side of it is, I suppose the other side of it is if you're not worrying about elite
sentences.zh: 我想问题的另一面在于，如果你担心的不是精英过剩，

sentences.en: overproduction, but you're worrying about you want to get the very best talented people into jobs, and into the top jobs.
sentences.zh: 而是希望让最有才华的人进入工作岗位，进入顶尖职位，

sentences.en: And if you want to do that, that would be good for everyone.
sentences.zh: 如果你想实现这一点，那对每个人都有好处。

sentences.en: Because if you have the most talented people in the top jobs, then they're hopefully going to run things more competently and make better decisions.
sentences.zh: 因为如果最优秀的人才占据了顶尖职位，他们有望更称职地管理事务，做出更明智的决策。

sentences.en: So that would be the alternative kind of sort of meritocratic argument that you do want the competition, you do want people competing,
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种替代性的精英管理论点，即你确实需要竞争，确实需要人们去角逐，

sentences.en: you want exams that do find who the most talented are, and do also, you know, give them the education they need.
sentences.zh: 你需要通过考试来发现谁是最有才华的人，同时也为他们提供所需的教育。

sentences.en: And that will be good for society.
sentences.zh: 这对社会是有益的。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, there's a difference, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这之间是有区别的，不是吗？

sentences.en: But I mean, just to go back to whether exams are an end in themselves, the more people are educated, the more they're in a position to create jobs.
sentences.zh: 我想回到“考试是否本身就是目的”这个问题上，受教育的人越多，他们就越有能力创造就业机会。

sentences.en: And so the economy grows.
sentences.zh: 这样经济就会增长。

sentences.en: That is absolute gibberish.
sentences.zh: 那简直是胡说八道。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: Because if everything is funneled through the prism of examinations, and, you know, there are certain kind of, I don't know, Oxbridge colleges or something,
sentences.zh: 因为如果一切都通过考试的棱镜来过滤，而且，你知道，还有某些牛剑学院之类的存在，

sentences.en: that's seen as the absolute end, then of course, there's a finite number.
sentences.zh: 如果那被视为终极目标，那么当然，名额是有限的。

sentences.en: But if people's education is better across the entire spectrum of society, then people have the knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但如果整个社会的教育水平都提高了，那么人们就拥有了知识。

sentences.en: Then the magic wand does appear.
sentences.zh: 那时，魔法棒就会出现了。

sentences.en: Tom Holland's magic wand.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰的魔法棒。

sentences.en: It's not magic.
sentences.zh: 那不是魔法。

sentences.en: It's sensible policies for a happier Britain.
sentences.zh: 那是为了一个更幸福的英国所采取的明智政策。

sentences.en: I am right.
sentences.zh: 我是对的。

sentences.en: You're wrong.
sentences.zh: 你是错的。

sentences.en: The best educated cabinet we ever had was the Wilson government of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们有史以来受教育程度最高的内阁是20世纪60年代的威尔逊政府。

sentences.en: I mean, they're all Oxford dons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们全是牛津大学的学者。

sentences.en: They're all super educated.
sentences.zh: 他们都受过极好的教育。

sentences.en: Now, nobody, I mean, not even, they're not even their greatest fans, points to that government and says...
sentences.zh: 现在，没人，甚至连他们最忠实的粉丝，都不会指着那个政府说……

sentences.en: No, but you're looking at it again through the prism of elites, through people going to Oxbridge.
sentences.zh: 不，你又是在通过精英的棱镜，通过那些去牛剑的人的视角来看待这个问题。

sentences.en: That's not the point.
sentences.zh: 重点不在这里。

sentences.en: The point is that if you look at it, you know, there are exams you have to do.
sentences.zh: 重点是，如果你仔细观察，你知道，有些考试是你必须参加的。

sentences.en: There are certain exams you do spectacularly well.
sentences.zh: 有些考试你必须考得非常出色。

sentences.en: You get the best prizes.
sentences.zh: 你才能获得最好的奖项。

sentences.en: That's the Chinese system.
sentences.zh: 那是中国的制度。

sentences.en: I mean, that's often...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那通常是……

sentences.en: If you look at things entirely through the prism of getting to universities, that's how we would look at it.
sentences.zh: 如果你完全通过“进入大学”这个棱镜来看待事物，那确实是我们看待它的方式。

sentences.en: But there is another way of saying that you take away the whole apparatus of exaMs. And it's about learning.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种说法，即抛弃整个考试体系。这关乎学习。

sentences.en: It's about knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这关乎知识。

sentences.en: And it's about getting skills and understanding and perspectives that then enable you to kind of create your own context.
sentences.zh: 这关乎获取技能、理解力和视角，从而使你能够创造属于自己的环境。

sentences.en: I think that's a really interesting point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常有趣的观点。

sentences.en: I'm going to throw something else into the mix here.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点。

sentences.en: It was another sort of China and John Stuart Mill point, which is when they were talking about exams for the civil service in the 19th century, John Stuart Mill said,
sentences.zh: 这是另一个关于中国和约翰·斯图尔特·密尔的观点，当他们在19世纪讨论公务员考试时，密尔曾说，

sentences.en: I wouldn't want the best and brightest in the civil service.
sentences.zh: 我不希望最优秀、最聪明的人都去当公务员。

sentences.en: He said, if the exams meant that all of the best and brightest went to work in the civil service, that would be terrible.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果考试意味着所有最优秀、最聪明的人都去公务员系统工作，那将是可怕的。

sentences.en: And he said it would be terrible because you would then have nobody outside the civil service will kind of have the capacity
sentences.zh: 他说这很可怕，因为这样一来，公务员系统之外就没人有能力

sentences.en: to solve their problems because you just have everyone in the civil service kind of doing it.
sentences.zh: 去解决他们的问题了，因为所有人都挤在公务员系统里做这件事。

sentences.en: He also then said that you wouldn't have anyone with the capacity to check they were doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 他还说，这样就不会有人有能力去监督他们是否在做正确的事。

sentences.en: So how would you check if there was any corruption or anything?
sentences.zh: 那么，你该如何检查是否存在腐败或其他问题呢？

sentences.en: And he also said, and this is his China, and he also talks about Russia, is that the problem you would have is you would have like a self-perpetuating oligarchy.
sentences.zh: 他还说——这是他提到的中国，他也谈到了俄国——你面临的问题将是一个自我延续的寡头政治。

sentences.en: And in some senses, when exam systems get too good, and again, you could argue this for China,
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，当考试制度变得过于完善时，同样，你可以用这个观点来论证中国的情况，

sentences.en: they do become self-perpetuating.
sentences.zh: 它们确实会变得自我延续。

sentences.en: And it gets really, really hard to bring in any reform and change the content on what you're being examined.
sentences.zh: 而且要进行任何改革、改变考试内容变得非常非常困难。

sentences.en: That's the argument behind Michael Young's book about the rise of the meritocracy.
sentences.zh: 这就是迈克尔·杨关于《精英制度的崛起》一书背后的论点。

sentences.en: So he's the person who, Toby Young's father, wrote the 1945 Labour Manifesto.
sentences.zh: 他就是托比·杨的父亲，曾撰写了1945年的工党宣言。

sentences.en: He effectively coined the phrase meritocracy.
sentences.zh: 他实际上创造了“精英制度”（meritocracy）这个词。

sentences.en: But he was talking about that as a warning.
sentences.zh: 但他当时是把它作为一个警告提出来的。

sentences.en: He was saying you create this elite of meritocrats who are very, very well educated, who then think, you know,
sentences.zh: 他说，你创造了这样一群受过极好教育的精英，他们会认为，你知道，

sentences.en: they're different from aristocracies or oligarchies because they think, I earned this.
sentences.zh: 他们不同于贵族或寡头，因为他们认为：这是我挣来的。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: I'm morally better than other people because I worked so hard and I'm so clever.
sentences.zh: 我比别人道德上更优越，因为我工作如此努力，而且我如此聪明。

sentences.en: And that argument is around a lot in politics at the moment that we've created, that there is this sort of self-conscious
sentences.zh: 这种论点在当前的政治中非常普遍，即我们创造了，存在着这样一种自我意识强烈的

sentences.en: middle class, highly educated, meritocratic elite, you know, the winners and losers of society,
sentences.zh: 中产阶级、受过高等教育的精英阶层，你知道，社会的赢家和输家，

sentences.en: you know, who think that they are not just luckier and cleverer than other people, but they are morally
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们认为自己不仅比别人更幸运、更聪明，而且在道德上

sentences.en: more deserving because they earned it through their own efforts, through passing exams, through precisely this point.
sentences.zh: 更值得拥有这一切，因为这是他们通过自己的努力、通过通过考试挣来的，正是基于这一点。

sentences.en: You know what this entire episode shows?
sentences.zh: 你知道这一整集节目说明了什么吗？

sentences.en: That we've just degenerated into a rambling.
sentences.zh: 说明我们已经沦落到胡言乱语的地步了。

sentences.en: No, what it shows is that there is almost no topic more calculated to generate argument and disagreement and intense feelings on the subject of exaMs. And Dominic, I'm going to...
sentences.zh: 不，这说明在考试这个话题上，几乎没有比这更能引发争论、分歧和强烈情绪的议题了。多米尼克，我要……

sentences.en: Yeah, you're going to have the last word.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让你做最后的总结。

sentences.en: You're going to have the last word.
